title: Wipe the plate rim, holding the plate
instruction: Clean up the plate's rim with the towel pad before the plate goes out to the guest.
context: Plating guides tell cooks to clean the rim before a plate goes out: Culinary Arts Switzerland says to wipe the rim with a damp cloth before serving, Chefitt to wipe the plate edge before it leaves the kitchen, and the caterer Personal Touch Dining to wipe every rim before sending a plate out (there one cook polishes, wiping off drips). The arranged food in the middle must stay untouched while the rim is wiped. Here the plate stands on a wet stainless-steel pass, and wet porcelain on wet steel slides when a towel is dragged across the rim: with the same wiping and nobody holding the plate, the recorded run scored 0 because the plate slid away under the towel. So one arm has to hold the plate still by its rim while the other wipes. The instruction says only to clean the rim with the towel pad; it does not say to hold the plate or to keep off the food. Done by: cooks and chefs at the pass of a restaurant kitchen, and catering cooks, before each plate is sent out.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Pass: a wet stainless-steel shelf, 30 x 42 cm and 4 cm tall, centred at x 24, y 0 (fixed). Plate: 0.45 kg porcelain, square, 23.6 x 23.6 cm, standing on the pass centred at x 24, y 0: a 1 cm thick base with a raised lip round its edge, 1.6 cm wide and 1.2 cm tall, and inside the lip a flat rim band 3.7 cm wide. Three sauce smudges, 3 x 3 cm (visual only), on the rim band 8.35 cm from the plate's centre: near side (x 15.65, y 0), right side (x 24, y -8.35) and far-right (x 29.9, y -5.9). Food: meat, mash and greens in the middle of the plate (visual only); the scorer's food box is 7 x 7 cm, centred on the plate, and 4 cm tall from the top of the base. Towel pad: a damp folded towel, 0.03 kg, 3 x 3 x 2.5 cm, lying on a steel stand 5 x 5 cm and 3 cm tall at x 15, y -24.
scoring: Every step, from poses and the towel-plate contact force; the score at the end counts. A step rubs a smudge when the towel pad's centre is within 2 cm (horizontally, in the plate's frame) of the smudge's centre, the towel presses on the plate with at least 0.8 N and it moves at least 1 cm/s relative to the plate. A smudge is clean after 10 rubbing steps (0.5 s at the 0.05 s step) in total. 1.0: all three smudges clean, with the plate kept within 1 cm and 5 degrees of where it was when the towel first touched it (the grip on the lip may nudge it before then). Otherwise one third per clean smudge (0.33, 0.67), capped at 0.5 if the plate slid more than 1 cm or turned more than 5 degrees once the towel touched it. 0 from the moment the plate is more than 3 cm from its start, is lifted more than 2 cm, or anything comes near the food: a finger pad of either arm within 1 cm of the food box, or the towel pad overlapping it.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the plate back in the middle of the pass and the towel pad back on its stand. In a real trial, put three fresh sauce smudges on the rim and wet the pass and the towel again.
fidelity: Rigid boxes (a square plate, a rigid towel pad); the towel-plate contact force is read each step. Liquids are not simulated: the wet pass and damp towel are friction settings (0.02 steel, 0.10 plate base, 0.8 pad), so a pressed, dragged towel pushes an unheld plate. The smudges are visual and stay, so cleaning counts the steps in which the towel rubs each smudge with at least 0.8 N while moving relative to the plate. The food has no collision: a keep-out box over the plate's middle stands in.
